title: Event Ticket Calculator
prompt:
The following program is intended to calculate the final price of an event purchase and apply one discount based on the subtotal. The program produces incorrect totals and discount categories. Fix it.

The corrected program should calculate the subtotal as ticket price multiplied by number of tickets, select only the highest discount level earned, subtract the discount, add the service fee, and print the correct totals.
starter_code:
ticket_price = float(input("Price of one ticket: "))
tickets = int(input("Number of tickets: "))
service_fee = float(input("Service fee: "))

subtotal = ticket_price + tickets

if subtotal >= 50:
    discount = subtotal * 0.05
elif subtotal >= 100:
    discount = subtotal * 0.10
elif subtotal >= 200:
    discount = subtotal * 0.15
else:
    discount = 0

final_total = subtotal - discount * service_fee

print("Subtotal:", round(subtotal, 2))
print("Discount:", round(discount, 2))
print("Final total:", round(final_total, 2))

rover_y = int(input("Rover y: "))

extended_grabber = int(input("Extended grabber range: "))
scanner = int(input("Scanner range: "))

sample_radius = sample_diameter / 2

Fix the code while keeping the function signature; do not change values. The system grades corrected code against hidden tests. An optional brief explanation of the defect can be recorded separately.

title: Explain an Inclusive Range Count
prompt: Study the function that counts storage readings inside [low, high]. For values = [3, 5, 7, 9], low = 5, high = 7, answer four short numbered parts: (1) what the function returns in general; (2) the running count after each reading and final result; (3) why it includes both boundaries; (4) what happens for empty values and for low > high. Write explanations rather than editing code. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Create Game-Point Records
prompt: Each game has a nonnegative point total. Complete makePointRecords(amounts, cap) to return one new PointRecord object per value, in order. Each object must hold amount (the original integer) and counted (the smaller of amount and cap). PointRecord is supplied. Return an empty list when amounts is empty; do not change amounts or reuse one object for multiple entries.

title: Create Donation Excess Records
prompt: A donation drive needs to see when a contribution exceeds its per-group allowance. Complete makeDonationRecords(amounts, cap). Return a separate DonationRecord for each nonnegative input amount, in order. Store the original value in amount and the amount ABOVE cap in excess (0 when amount <= cap). DonationRecord is supplied. Do not change amounts, and return an empty list for an empty input.

title: Fix Contribution Object Storage
prompt: An event needs a separate record for each contribution. The method must return objects containing amount (original value) and counted (at most cap). One logic defect causes incorrect returned entries. Correct the program; input order must remain unchanged and every entry must be an independent object. Optional bug explanation is recorded separately.

title: Explain How Activity Objects Are Created
prompt: Read the object-creation code with amounts = [2, 8, 4] and cap = 5. Explain in four numbered parts: (1) the returned container and its element type; (2) each object's (amount, counted) values; (3) why a new object must be created inside the loop; (4) behavior for empty input and an amount exactly equal to cap. Keep answers concise. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Find the Longest Successful Run
prompt: Each PracticeRound in records has Boolean successful, and records are ordered by time. Write longestSuccessRun(records) to return the length of the longest consecutive run of successful=true. A false value ends the current run. Return 0 for empty input or when nothing succeeded. Do not modify the records or return a starting index.

title: Find the Longest Daily Reading Streak
prompt: Each ReadingDay record has a nonnegative pagesRead attribute. A day qualifies when pagesRead >= minimum. Write longestReadingRun(records, minimum) to find the longest consecutive sequence of qualifying days in time order. A nonqualifying day breaks a run. Return 0 for empty records or no qualifying days. Do not mutate the objects.

title: Fix the Longest Successful Run
prompt: The practice tracker must report the longest consecutive run of successful=true objects. false breaks the run and empty input returns 0. One logic defect incorrectly carries a failed round forward. Fix only the necessary logic and keep the function signature unchanged. Submit corrected code; optional reflection is unscored.

title: Explain a Longest Study Streak
prompt: Study the code with completed values [true, true, false, true] in time order. Answer in four short numbered parts: (1) what the returned number means; (2) current and longest after each day; (3) why false resets current but leaves longest alone; (4) what is returned for empty records or all-false records. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Count Days With Higher Attendance
prompt: Each AttendanceRecord contains integer before and after values. Write countAttendanceIncreases(records) to count records whose after value is strictly greater than before. Equal values are not increases. Return 0 for no records; read attributes from the same object and do not modify any object.

title: Calculate Total Sales Increase
prompt: Each SalesRecord has integer before and after daily sales. Write totalSalesIncrease(records) to sum only positive increases (after - before) across all records. A decrease or no change contributes 0. For example, changes +3, 0, -2 contribute a total increase of 3. Return 0 for no records. Leave the objects unchanged.

title: Fix the Strict Increase Count
prompt: A tracker must count only records whose later reading exceeds its earlier reading. Equal values do not qualify. The code has one comparison error. Correct it without changing the signature or the objects. Empty input returns 0. Submit corrected code; optional reflection is unscored.

title: Explain a Record Comparison
prompt: Using (before, after) values [(2,4), (8,8), (3,1)], answer briefly: (1) what is counted; (2) count after each record and returned value; (3) why before and after must come from the same object; (4) how the result changes if >= replaces >. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Count Animal Sightings
prompt: Each supplied Animal object has name and nonnegative integer numberSeen. Write countAnimalSightings(records, minimum) to count how many records have numberSeen >= minimum. Count records, not total sightings. Include equality. Return 0 for no records or no matches, and leave all objects unchanged.

title: Sum Visits for Qualifying Pets
prompt: Each Pet has name and a nonnegative integer visits count. Write totalQualifyingVisits(records, minimum). Add together the visits values of pets whose visits >= minimum, and ignore other pets. This returns total visits, NOT the number of pets. Include pets at the threshold. Return 0 for empty or no-qualifying input. Do not mutate the records.

title: Fix the Animal Threshold Count
prompt: The shelter must count Animal records with numberSeen >= minimum. Empty records count as 0. The code wrongly excludes animals seen exactly minimum times. Correct the logic; do not sum sightings or change records. Submit corrected code; optional reflection is unscored.

title: Explain an Object Threshold Count
prompt: Read countVisitRecords with visits values [2, 5, 7] and minimum = 5. Explain in four short numbered parts: (1) whether the program counts records or totals visits; (2) matches after each item and the returned result; (3) why it compares record.visits rather than the whole object; (4) result with > replacing >= and result for empty records. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Count Years That Meet Two Digit Rules
prompt: Each YearRecord has a four-digit integer year. Write countDisplayYears(records). A year qualifies only when its tens and ones digits sum to AT LEAST 10 AND its ones digit is even. Extract digits using integer / and % (division and remainder), not string conversion. Count qualifying objects, not the years. Return 0 for empty records; do not mutate objects.

title: Count Label Codes Meeting a Target
prompt: Each CodeRecord has a four-digit integer code. Write countLabelCodes(records, target). Count each record whose tens and ones digits add up to EXACTLY target AND whose ones digit is odd. Extract both digits using integer arithmetic, not text conversion. target is an integer from 0 to 18. Return 0 for empty records and do not modify the objects.

title: Fix the Digit Rule Boundary
prompt: An archive counts YearRecord objects only when the final two digits sum to at least 10 AND the last digit is even. Each year is 1000-9999. The function has one incorrect inequality and misses boundary cases. Fix its logic without changing the interface or converting digits to strings. Submit corrected code; optional reflection is unscored.

title: Explain the Digit-Rule Count
prompt: Read countLibraryCodes using codes [2748, 2747, 2746]. Answer four short numbered parts: (1) both digit rules; (2) tens and ones digits and running count after each code; (3) why AND is required rather than OR; (4) whether 2746 qualifies and what empty input returns. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Build an Alternating Banner
prompt: Write makeBanner(n), where n is 0-6. Produce one string with n left-aligned rows. For row i starting at 1, print i copies of '#' if i is odd, otherwise i copies of '+'. Use a row loop and an inner repetition loop, and put exactly one newline between rows, with no trailing newline or spaces. If n=0, return an empty string.

title: Build a Descending Decoration
prompt: Write makeDecoration(n), where n is 0-6. Produce n rows in one string. Row 1 has n '*' symbols, row 2 has (n-1) '-' symbols, row 3 has (n-2) '*' symbols, and so on until the last row contains one symbol. Use an outer row loop and an inner repetition loop. Separate rows by exactly one newline, with no spaces or trailing newline. Return '' if n=0.

title: Fix the Alternating Row Symbols
prompt: A festival requires row i to contain i copies of '#' on odd rows and '+' on even rows. n is 0-6. Rows are separated by one newline, with no trailing newline. The code chooses symbols for the wrong parity. Correct only the logic while preserving the nested loops and output contract. Submit corrected code; optional reflection is unscored.

title: Explain Nested Alternating Rows
prompt: Study makeMarkerRows with n=3. Answer four short numbered parts: (1) how many symbols each row gets and which symbol it uses; (2) exact returned string with newlines represented as \n; (3) what the outer and inner loops do; (4) why no newline is added before row 1 and what happens at n=0. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Add Quiz Points From Time
prompt: Each QuizRound has nonnegative seconds and Boolean correct. Write totalQuizPoints(rounds) to total points. Incorrect rounds earn 0. A correct round earns 3 if seconds < 2; 2 if 2 <= seconds < 4; 1 if seconds >= 4. Include times exactly at 2 and 4 in the proper intervals. Return 0 for an empty collection. No timer construction or mutation.

title: Add Challenge Points From Attempts
prompt: Each ChallengeRound has a positive integer attempts and Boolean correct. Write totalChallengePoints(rounds). Incorrect rounds earn 0, regardless of attempts. Correct answers earn 3 points if solved on attempt 1, 2 points if solved on attempt 2, and 1 point for attempt 3 or later. Sum all points; empty rounds returns 0. The attempts have already been recorded; do not simulate retries.

title: Fix the Two-Second Scoring Boundary
prompt: A quiz awards 3 points for a correct answer with seconds < 2; 2 points when 2 <= seconds < 4; 1 point when seconds >= 4; and 0 when incorrect. The faulty code includes exactly 2 seconds in the wrong tier. Correct the logic without changing the interface, and return 0 for empty rounds. Submit corrected code; optional reflection is unscored.

title: Explain the Tiered Quiz Total
prompt: Read totalTeamPoints with rounds [(seconds=1.0, correct=true), (2.0, true), (1.0, false)]. Answer four short numbered parts: (1) scoring rules; (2) awarded points and running total for every round; (3) why time checks appear inside the correctness test; (4) what happens at exactly 4 seconds for a correct round and for an empty list. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Update a Game Score Within Bounds
prompt: A Game object has score initially 0 and nonnegative goal. Write updateGameScore(game, changes) to apply EVERY integer change in order, adjusting game.score after EACH change so that score never stays below 0 or above goal. Clamp an invalid score to the nearest bound, then continue with later changes. Return the final stored score. Do not alter game.goal. For empty changes return 0.

title: Update a Storage Level by Rejecting Invalid Changes
prompt: A Storage object has level initially 0 and nonnegative capacity. Write updateStorageLevel(storage, changes) to examine each integer change in order. Apply a change ONLY if level + change is within [0, capacity]; otherwise reject that individual change and leave level as it was. Continue to process later changes. Return final storage.level and leave capacity unchanged. Empty changes returns 0. NOTE: This task rejects invalid changes; it does not clamp values.

title: Fix the Cumulative Score Update
prompt: A Game starts with score 0, goal nonnegative, and list changes (possibly negative). Apply changes cumulatively in order, clamping after each addition to [0, goal]. Continue even after reaching the goal. The faulty function replaces the running score rather than adding to it. Correct the code and preserve game.goal. Submit corrected code; optional reflection is unscored.

title: Explain Bounded Score Changes
prompt: Read updateTeamScore with score initially 0, goal 10, and changes [6, -3, 8, -2]. Explain in four short numbered parts: (1) which attribute changes and what is returned; (2) stored score after every change; (3) why bounds are checked after each individual change; (4) whether -2 is applied after the goal is reached and what happens for empty changes. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.

title: Create Number-Row Objects
prompt: For n from 0 to 6, makeNumberRows(n) returns one distinct NumberRow per row 1..n, in order. Each object stores number=i and text equal to the numbers 1 through i separated by ONE space, with no leading/trailing spaces. Use nested loops to build each row string. NumberRow class is supplied. Return an empty list for n=0. Objects must not alias one another.

title: Create Multiplication Stair Objects
prompt: For n from 0 to 6, makeStairLevels(n) returns one different StairLevel per level i=1..n. Each stores number=i and text containing the multiples i, 2*i, ..., i*i, separated by single spaces. Example: for level 3 the text is '3 6 9'. Use an outer loop over levels and inner loop over multipliers. StairLevel is supplied. Return an empty list for n=0, and do not reuse an object.

title: Fix the Reused Row Object
prompt: For n=0..6, makeLessonRows(n) must return a distinct NumberRow object for each row i. Each has number=i and text '1 2 ... i' with single spaces and no leading/trailing spaces. The faulty code appends multiple references to the same object. Fix the location of object creation; return an empty list for n=0. Submit corrected code; optional reflection is unscored.

title: Explain How Row Objects Are Stored
prompt: Read makeLabelRows for n=3. Answer four short numbered parts: (1) what fields each returned object contains; (2) the ordered pairs (number,text) for all three rows; (3) roles of the two loops; (4) why a new object is needed per row and what n=0 returns. Answer using four short numbered parts; equivalent correct explanations receive credit.
